fields.statement: At 54c67b81, built go build -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza and used it by hand in a scratch git repo (RHIZA_* unset, fake rex on PATH, a no-agent plan workflow). With a milestone request whose run the daemon had drawn, run start --workflow plan --new 'Ship v4' --request <it> --autonomous without --milestone exited 2 with '--autonomous is refused on a plan run that plans a milestone: milestone planning needs the owner, even in autonomous mode' (usage), queued, --foreground, --dry-run --json and via api call run.start; with --milestone too. No draft and no .git/rhiza/runs were written. The same request without --autonomous ran to succeeded with a journal not autonomous; a feature request's --request --autonomous run succeeded with autonomous true. run start <record change set> --autonomous and --new --milestone --autonomous each exited 2 the same way with change ls unchanged; after editing the milestone run's journal to autonomous:true, run resume exited 2 with the rule. The cycle-1 gap (milestone request kind not checked) is fixed. Scoped testscripts run-start-milestone-autonomous, plan-requests, plan-workflow-autonomous(-left) pass.

At 54c67b81, with the built binary in a scratch repo, rhiza.autonomy.plan=auto, queued a milestone request 'Ship v6' and a bug 'Crash on save' and ran rhiza daemon --permission-mode manual --max-runs 2 --once (RHIZA_TEST_NOW and RHIZA_TEST_DETACH_LOG set so nothing spawned). The detach log shows 'run start --foreground --workflow plan --new Ship v6 --request <id> --permission-mode manual --milestone' with no --autonomous, and 'run start ... --new Fix Crash on save ... --autonomous'. Starting a milestone request's run as the daemon does leaves its journal with no autonomous:true.
